reason: Paper 1 builds and tests a new pipeline: an inverse-dynamics labeller that turns unlabeled screen-recording videos into 1.52M agent steps. Pretraining on that data gives controlled gains over the same SFT recipe (OSWorld-Verified 9.3 to 14.1/15.8, AgentNetBench 64.1 to 69.3), and the gains grow with data scale. Its main weaknesses are a single base model, thin labeller evaluation and no comparison against other data sources. Paper 2 only runs three existing dataset-distillation methods on noisy CIFAR/Tiny-ImageNet and compares them with plain cross-entropy training on the noisy data. It has no noisy-label-learning baselines (e.g. DivideMix, co-teaching), its 'corollaries' are loose and unproven, and it admits the approach fails on asymmetric noise. So it offers no new method and little rigorous evidence.
recognized: W5: VideoAgentTrek (title recognized as a 2025 arXiv preprint; judged on merits)
